title: ServiceAccountRecord
description: One registered service account (a machine identity authenticated by an X-API-Key secret). The `subject` IS the API-key tenant string and the authorization subject, so a service account can own collections, receive shares and join groups under that one identifier — naming it as a share grantee or group member takes the explicit `@service:<subject>` form, which is what keeps the subject colon-free (a bare value is qualified to `bvbrc:<value>`, a federated identity the account can never authenticate as). It is colon-free by construction: ':' is reserved for federated 'issuer:sub' identities so the two namespaces stay disjoint, and the reserved tenants 'default' and 'public' are refused outright (a shared fallback tenant is not one caller's identity, and disabling it would lock out every unmapped key). This record NEVER carries key material, a key prefix, or a key count: the key<->account mapping lives only in the server's environment and is never surfaced by the API (same contract as /v1/config). `last_seen_at` is deliberately absent — the API-key auth path writes nothing back, so it would be permanently empty.

subject.description: The account's subject: its API-key tenant and its authorization identity. Colon-free.

purpose.description: Free text recorded at creation: what this credential is for. Empty string when not supplied.

created_by.description: Subject of the admin who registered the account.

disabled_by.description: Subject of the admin who LAST disabled the account; empty string if it has never been disabled. This is HISTORY, not state: it SURVIVES a re-enable (ADR-0004 decision 6 — the audit trail is the point), so a row that was revoked once never reads back identical to one that never was. Read `active` for the current state.

disabled_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of that last disable; empty string if never disabled. Kept across a re-enable — see `disabled_by`.

enabled_by.description: Subject of the admin who LAST re-enabled the account; empty string if it has never been re-enabled.

enabled_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of that last re-enable; empty string if never re-enabled.

active.description: The account's current state, and the ONLY field to read for it (never `disabled_at != ""`, which is now audit history). True when the account is not disabled. Disabling is a soft, best-effort revoke: the API-key auth path rejects a disabled account's key with 401 within the server's disabled-check cache TTL, and FAILS OPEN if the store cannot answer. The authoritative revoke is removing the key from the server environment and restarting.
